newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Noyabrskneftegaz plans share issue to pay taxes.
newsitem.headline: Noyabrskneftegaz plans share issue to pay taxes.

text.p: Russian oil company AOOT Noyabrskneftegaz plans to raise capital by issuing shares to pay off its tax debts, a spokesman for Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.

Andrei Trapeznikov told Reuters that Pyotr Mostovoi, head of the Federal Bankruptcy Agency, had told a government commission that the government had accepted a proposal by Noyabrskneftegaz to settle its debts by selling new shares.
Noyabrskneftegaz is the main production unit of OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft), one of a dozen Russian vertically integrated oil companies.
Sibneft, which would neither confirm nor deny the share plan, owns 61 percent of Noyabrskneftegaz's ordinary shares and two percent of its preferred shares.
Noyabrskneftegaz fell to $10.80 on the Russian Trading System after the news from $11.00 on Friday, the last day it was traded.
Noyabrskneftegaz owed a total of 1.47 trillion roubles ($255 million) in tax as of May 1, State Tax Service figures show.

In May, Noyabrskneftegaz shareholders approved a proposal to increase authorised but unissued capital by 30.83 trillion roubles from 15.71 billion roubles. Sibneft has said the shares will be issued proportionately to existing shareholders if they are issued as a result of an assets re-evaluation, but would be sold in other cases.
